items.requirement: Sized for about 49.7 A: the board's draw from the pack at the 6.0 V floor with the four TPS55285 at 6.35 A, nominal at an assumed 90 %. Round 1 sized both for 12.23 A (V90). No pack disconnect passed round 1: its one shortlisted candidate, R5460N212AF-TR-FE, failed the open balance lead (V107) in FU-B1, and FU-B3 found none. Answered under Raised by P1: V295: As V294: 3.3 V a cell under load is the lowest trip, the threshold set above it by the IC's accuracy band. V95's ±75 mV, round 1's R5460 figure, is no requirement (owner, 2026-10-02) V297: One IC does the pack disconnect, the pack overcurrent protection, the bench pack balance lead and the pack temperature, selected in FU-2F (owner, 2026-10-02) V301: 10 µA stays, with an operator wake contact for a start from the pack alone. The open-lead behaviour may rest on the IC's undervoltage logic, an inference. A bench test confirms it before the pages call V107 met: mid wire open, with and without a charger, and first cell attach (owner, 2026-10-02) V317: 12 µA. A disconnected pack loses about 8.6 mAh in 30 days. The 1 MOhm pull-down and its open-lead inference stay, for the bench test of V301 (owner, 2026-10-02) V319: A 12 V supply or a 4S LiPo pack (16.8 V full, about 12 to 13.2 V empty): 12 to 18 V, in place of 12 to 20 V. The overvoltage cut-off trips above 18 V; the research states its trip and release bands, the DC path current at 12 and 18 V, and whether an 18 V-class TVS behind the cut-off holds the bus at or under 27 V beside the bus capacitance of V318. The input still survives 25.2 V in either polarity (V83, V267) (owner, 2026-10-03)

items.requirement: Switches each of the 20 ports from 0.8 V (V55) to 8.4 V. The TPS259474LRPWR takes VIN only from 2.7 V. Answered under Raised by P1: V126: Only while the port is off, with the pin up to 12 V. While it is on, the switch conducts both ways: a braking servo drives current back into the rail, and a diode in the path would leave the servo's supply to rise until it fails. An ESC's BEC on an enabled port feeds the rail too; it is used with its BEC wire off, a current limitation (owner, 2026-10-02) V133: The capacitance is not known. The 2.35 A peak, the rail's 6.35 A limit less the 4.0 A two synchronised ports may draw, is a reported figure, not a pass or fail requirement (owner, 2026-10-02) V282: From 0.8 V the switch turns on and carries the port's current. The 3.0 A and the 570 mV this question names apply from 5.0 V up; below 5.0 V the drop is a reported figure, not a requirement (owner, 2026-10-01) V302: Yes. The search covers topologies that split the function across parts: a load switch from 0.5 V with separate reverse blocking, current limit and 20 V protection (owner, 2026-10-02) V312: A research run names the switch (TLP3545A first) and its current limit (INA301A1IDGKR on the port shunt first) as functions and verifies each, with the servo supply temperature latch's enable gate and power-up reset, before FU-2P56. No reverse-blocking part: V126 (owner, 2026-10-02)

items.requirement: The continuous current one TPS55285 with its heatsink holds at 6.0 V in and 50 °C ambient, in A. This is each rail's continuous rating (owner, 2026-09-30). The heatsink's size is round 3's. Answered under Raised by P1: V279: 72.0 °C beside a servo converter and 66.25 °C beside the adjustable supply's converter: the junction stays at 125 °C or below at the 8 A typical inductor clamp. At 50 °C ambient without a heatsink a rail then holds about 2.47 A at 8.4 V from 6.0 V before it trips (owner, 2026-10-02) V281: 33 °C/W, the datasheet's RθJA on TI's 4-layer 2 oz EVM (SLVSI72A 5.3). The heatsink adds margin, which round 3 sizes (owner, 2026-10-01) V283: The rail's own latch: only that converter switches off, and it stays off until the operator clear control (F11) clears it. The other rails and the ESC keep running, and the firmware reports the trip (owner, 2026-10-01) V303: A latch part a research run selects, 4 a board; R3's 74LVC1G175GW,125 is the first candidate, SN74LVC1G74DCUR beside it (owner, 2026-10-02) V315: A research run before FU-2P56 reads whether the TPS55285 takes current back into its output and passes it to its input (forced-PWM operation), and researches a clamp on each servo rail and on the adjustable supply's output that holds it under its ceiling, stating the energy the clamp absorbs. The energy a servo returns is not known unless a servo data sheet states it (owner, 2026-10-02) V316: An active shunt clamp that tracks the set voltage, behind an ideal diode. An ideal-diode controller and its MOSFET sit between the converter's output and the rail, so back-fed current cannot reach the converter. The signal that turns the MOSFET off when the rail rises above the converter's output also enables the clamp: an op-amp then switches a load resistor across the rail once the rail exceeds the voltage before the MOSFET by 0.1 V, an offset that resistors set. The research states the MOSFET's drop and loss at the rail's current, where the converter's feedback is taken, the controller's turn-off signal and time, and the margin to the port ceiling's lowest trip edge (owner, 2026-10-02)

items.function: input transient clamp (TVS on the DC input and on the pack input)
items.requirement: No part in FU-2B1; P2 returned no entry for it. The reverse-polarity protection, the overvoltage protection, the inrush limiting and the source selection survive 60 V for 10 µs only behind the clamp: TVS2701DRBR clamps to 35.7 V at 27 °C and 37.3 V at 125 °C. The clamp is the power input's protection, researched in stage 1, with TVS2701DRBR as its first candidate (owner, 2026-10-02). Behind the overvoltage cut-off the bus sees the clamp voltage for 3.98 µs typical, 5.4 µs maximum, plus the MOSFETs' gate-discharge time, against the TPS55285's 27 V absolute maximum. Answered under Raised by P1: V308: A second clamp on the bus behind the cut-off, ahead of the TPS55285, holds their input pins at or under 27 V. A P2-P4 follow-up of R5 and R7 researches it before FU-2P56, and states how the BQ40Z80 pack pins stay at or under 35 V (owner, 2026-10-02)
items.source: FU-2B1, R5 P2 report and P4 checks

items.function: bus clamp (behind the overvoltage cut-off, ahead of the TPS55285)
items.requirement: The DC input takes 12 to 18 V (V319, owner, 2026-10-03), so the overvoltage cut-off trips above 18 V and its highest trip falls from 22.0 V. Two ways hold the TPS55285 inputs at or under 27 V for the cut-off window, both to be read: the bus capacitance, with no clamp part (V318): state the minimum capacitance, effective at the bus voltage, that does so from the new highest trip for 5.4 µs maximum plus the gate discharge at 27 A, and at 36.7 A as a sensitivity, a stage 2 requirement; and an 18 V-class flat-clamp TVS on the bus behind the cut-off (TVS1800DRVR first, which FU-2H dropped only because its breakdown sat under the 22.0 V trip): its breakdown minimum against the new highest trip and its clamp at 27 A against 27 V. The input TVS2701DRBR stays for the 25.2 V either-polarity survival (V83, V267)
items.source: V308, V318, V319, V83, V267; FU-2H, R5 P2 report and drops of the bus clamp
items.reason: the owner's rulings of 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-03 on FU-2H (Raised by P1, V316 to V319)

items.function: Servo rail clamp; Servo rail clamp reference; servo rail ideal diode (new)
items.requirement: On each of the 3 servo rails and on the adjustable supply's output (up to 15 V): an ideal-diode controller and its MOSFET between the converter's output and the rail, so back-fed current cannot reach the converter; the signal that turns the MOSFET off when the rail rises above the converter's output also enables the clamp; an op-amp then switches a load resistor across the rail once the rail exceeds the voltage before the MOSFET by 0.1 V, an offset that resistors set (V316, owner, 2026-10-02). State the MOSFET's drop and loss at the rail's current (up to 6.35 A), where the converter's feedback is taken, the controller's turn-off signal and its time, the energy and peak current the clamp absorbs, and the margin to the port ceiling's lowest trip edge. FU-2H's REF3112AIDBZR reference was verified; its OPA376AIDBVR and TLV9001IDBVR failed the adjustable supply's 15 V
items.source: V126, V315, V316; FU-2H, R6 P2 report and ledger

found_values.value: The INA228 the display's settings name fills BENCH page 0x20 registers 0 (voltage) and 1 (current): with ina228_en on, the INA228 at the ina228_addr address (0x40, 0x41, 0x44 or 0x45; 0x44 or 0x45 beside the INA3221s) whenever it answers; the ESC telemetry fills them when ina228_en is off or that monitor does not answer. Both INA228s answer their addresses in every test, because the acknowledge depends only on the A0/A1 pins and the address byte (SLYS021A 7.5.1), so an answer cannot tell the cabled path; the operator sets ina228_addr to the cabled path's monitor (the two paths replace each other, IOBoard.md:442) and ina228_shunt to its shunt. ina228_shunt takes 0.1 to 20 mOhm in 0.1 steps: the onboard 200 uOhm and the external 100 uOhm can be entered, 50 uOhm cannot. Applied to Motor monitor as 'reading of record'
found_values.source: checkout 5f5c0a61: shared/settings/settings.c:29 (k_ina_addr), :87-95 (ina228_en, ina228_addr 'Set by its A0 and A1 pins', ina228_shunt 0.1 to 20 mOhm); hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:442, :503; firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:705-727 (telemetry the only source on the bring-up module); docs/OpenYGE.md:380-381; INA228 SLYS021A 7.5.1, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina228.pdf

At the shunts' upper tolerance the trips fall to 148.5 A (BVR +1 %) and 285.7 A (BAS +5 %). Applied to Motor monitor as 'overcurrent alert threshold'

found_values.value: One averaged INA228 reading above SOVL trips. SLOWALERT 1, AVG 4, VSHCT and VBUSCT 1052 us, MODE Bh (continuous shunt and bus): one averaged result each 4 x 2 x 1.052 = 8.42 ms, 8.50 ms at the -1 % oscillator. ALERT asserts within 2 results, 17.0 ms, of the crossing, inside the 20 ms of IOBoard.md:113. The reset ADC_CONFIG (MODE Fh) gives 12.6 ms a result, so the mode is written. Two consecutive conversions apply to temperatures only (V288)
found_values.source: IOBoard.md:113; INA228 SLYS021A 6.5 (conversion time field 5h = 1052 us), 7.3.4, Table 7-16 (SLOWALERT bit 13), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina228.pdf

found_values.source: Research.md V1, V288, F7, R3 row; IOBoard.md:113

The first INA3221 conversion wholly above 3.0 A completes within 3.63 + 1.21 = 4.84 ms of the crossing (three channels, shunt only, CT 100), inside one 5 ms sample of the tree's 200 Hz sensor; the critical line reaches the main coprocessor through the 74VHC21FT cascade in 20.5 ns max. The abort follows after the blanking time, which is not read (V287), plus the main coprocessor's action

found_values.source: IOBoard.md:113, :387; docs/Servo.md:35-36

found_values.value: VBUS from the external shunt's pack-side sense lead, tapped ahead of the IN+ series resistor; the voltage is measured at the pack. The INA228's VBUS input is 0.8 to 1.2 MOhm, 0 to 85 V. Its protection is stage 2's (V306)
found_values.source: docs/Screens.md:131-134; IOBoard.md:464, :509; Research.md V306; INA228 SLYS021A 6.5 (ZVBUS, VVBUS)

found_values.value: 85 V from either lead to ground and 85 V between the leads, either polarity: a lead on the wrong terminal or the load side shorted puts the pack across them; R3 clamps the pack node under 85 V. V306 sets the stage 2 protection to hold under 40 V between the leads, each input -0.3 to 85 V and 5 mA a pin through that fault, matching SLYS021A 6.1
found_values.source: IOBoard.md:464; Research.md R3 row, F15, V306; INA228 SLYS021A 6.1

found_values.value: 0 A to the positive full scale; every current threshold in the servo code is positive
found_values.source: shared/servo/servo_limit.c:56-62; shared/servo/servo_sync.c:35-37

found_values.value: Thresholds: INA3221 critical 30.00 mV (3.0 A on 10 mOhm, 750 counts of 40 uV, each single conversion); warning 10.00 mV (1.0 A, 250 counts, averaged value, AVG 4); INA228 SOVL 30.00 mV (24,000 counts of 1.25 uV, ADCRANGE 1) on both paths. Latching: INA3221 critical and warning transparent (CEN 0, WEN 0, the reset state), because the main coprocessor times the lines and only a Mask/Enable read on the measurement coprocessor's bus clears a latch; INA228 ALERT latched (ALATCH 1), cleared by a DIAG_ALRT read at re-arm. Blanking time: not read. SBOS576C states when the transparent Critical pin pulls low (7.3.2.1) and not when it releases with three channels enabled; its only example enables CH1 alone (9.2.1, Table 9-1). If the pin holds until the same channel converts again, 5 ms lies between one refresh (3.63 ms max) and two (6.6 ms typ) and the abort fires; if the pin follows each conversion of any channel, a sustained overcurrent on one channel holds the line low about 1.1 ms in each 3.3 ms and no blanking above 1.21 ms fires. A bench measurement of the Critical pin with three channels enabled and one above the limit, or TI's statement, fixes it. Against the breaker: the blanking acts on 3.0 to 3.96 A only; from 3.96 to 4.84 A the port switch's breaker acts (owner)
found_values.source: IOBoard.md:113, :387, :389; docs/Servo.md:35-36; INA3221 SBOS576C 6.5, 7.3.2.1, 7.3.2.2, 9.2.1, 9.2.2, Mask/Enable register bits 10 and 11, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina3221.pdf; INA228 SLYS021A Table 7-16, 7.6.1.13; FU-2H adjudicator rulings 016 and 017

report.value: Not read. SBOS576C states that the transparent Critical pin pulls low when any channel's conversion exceeds its limit (7.3.2.1) and not when it releases with three channels enabled; its example enables CH1 alone (9.2.1, Table 9-1). Reading A, the pin holds until the same channel converts again: 5 ms lies between one refresh (3 channels, shunt only, CT 100: 3.3 ms typ, 3.63 ms max) and two (6.6 ms typ; no minimum conversion time stated), a single over-limit conversion is logged, two abort. Reading B, the pin follows each conversion of any channel: a sustained overcurrent on one channel holds the line low about 1.1 ms in each 3.3 ms and no blanking above 1.21 ms ever aborts. Fixed by a bench measurement of the Critical pin with three channels enabled and one above the limit, or by TI's statement. Until then the owner's blanking rule on the critical line is not shown to abort a sustained 3.0 to 3.96 A overcurrent; the firmware check at every 5 ms sample on the measurement coprocessor still does
report.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina3221.pdf SBOS576C 6.5, 7.3.2.1, 7.4.1, 9.2.1, 9.2.2, Figure 9-2, read 2026-10-03T00:15:40Z; test/host/test_servo_limit.c:19; IOBoard.md:113; FU-2H adjudicator rulings 016 and 017

found_values.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/bq40z80.pdf SLUSBV4D 5.5 (K, OE, GE rows); Research.md V294, V295

found_values.value: No source sets a lower bound. The maker forbids a cell under 3.3 V under load 'auch nicht kurzzeitig' (not even briefly), so the filter has an upper bound: the cell must not fall from the threshold to 3.3 V within it. That fall rate is not known (internal resistance not measured, V285). Taken: the shortest delay the IC allows, BQ40Z80 CUV:Delay 0 s in 1 s steps, which triggers on average within up to 1.5 s (TRM 3.1 note)
found_values.source: https://www.stefansliposhop.de/media/general/SLS_Sicherheitshinweise_DE_A4.pdf section 4; Research.md V285; https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/SLUUBT5 SLUUBT5C 3.1 (FU-2H reading, not re-read)

found_values.value: 12 uA at most from the pack while it is disconnected (V317, owner 2026-10-02, in place of V301's 10 uA), with an operator wake contact for a start from the pack alone (V301); a disconnected pack loses about 8.6 mAh in 30 days
found_values.source: Research.md V301, V317 Answers at 5f5c0a61c4f7

found_values.value: (b): the pack protection, one IC for the disconnect, the overcurrent protection, the balance lead and the pack temperature (V297, V298), its threshold in the IC's nonvolatile data flash, written once before the board ships. Not (c): a threshold firmware writes at each start-up is not in force before the firmware runs
found_values.source: Research.md V297, V298 Answers at 5f5c0a61c4f7; https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/bq40z80.pdf SLUSBV4D 1

found_values.value: 25 % on each rail, chosen: each rail part is rated at least 1.25 times its summed load. 3.3 V: 1,475 mA x 1.25 = 1.84 A. 5 V: 2.08 A x 1.25 = 2.60 A. It covers the R6, R7 and R8 parts not in the sum and loads stated as typical only
found_values.source: round1/FU-B3/002-P2-R5.json V99 (chosen value, confirmed by FU-B1, FU-2B1, FU-2F and FU-2H P4); round2/FU-2B1/003-P2-R5.json report

The load-cell excitation runs from R13's own regulator (V254) and the encoder's 5 V from the encoder converter (V108), so neither is on the 5 V rail; the board's own 5 V load is the TCAN1472VDRQ1 (VCC 4.5 V to 5.5 V); the encoder's 5 V position takes 5 VDC +/-5 % (E6B2-CWZ1X)

found_values.value: Either order. The one IO board part on both rails is the TCAN1472VDRQ1 (VCC 5 V, VIO 3.3 V), with undervoltage protection on both supplies and passive behaviour unpowered; the 5 V rail feeds the display through the TPS25947, which blocks reverse current

found_values.value: Yes, required: with the pack's power leads connected and its balance lead unplugged or one wire open, the disconnect holds the pack off, with and without a charger. found_values.source: Research.md V301, V317 Answers; F9 Answer at 5f5c0a61c4f7

found_values.value: The TPS55285 takes current back into its output and passes it to its input in FPWM only: 'The high-side N-MOSFET is not turned off even if the current through the MOSFET is zero. Thus, the inductor current changes its direction after it runs to zero. The power flow is from output side to input side' (6.4.1). In PFM, the default (MODE register 06h bit 1 = 0), it turns the switches off at zero current 'to prevent the reverse current from output to input' (6.4.2), so a returned current raises the rail. No reverse or negative current limit is stated in the data sheet. Input OVP, 22.0 to 23.0 V rising, stops switching when the input cannot sink the returned current (6.3.14). Output OVP at 110.5 to 120 % of the target (9.28 to 10.08 V at 8.4 V; 6.08 to 6.6 V at 5.5 V) lies above both ceilings. The energy a servo returns is not stated on the servo pages read (Savox SH-0255MG+, SB-2290SG): not known. With V316 an ideal diode sits between each converter and its rail, so no back-fed current reaches the converter and PFM stays its mode
found_values.source: SLVSI72A, ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf, read 2026-10-03T00:23:26Z 5.4, 6.3.14, 6.3.15, 6.4.1, 6.4.2, 7.6; Savox SH-0255MG+ (www.savox-servo.com/en/product/SH-0255MGplus/savox-servo-sh-0255mg-digital-dc-motor-metal-gear, vendors.py fetch HTTP 200, 2026-10-03T00:30:19Z) and SB-2290SG (www.savox-servo.com/en/product/SB-2290SG/savox-servo-sb-2290sg-digital-brushless-motor-steel-gear-high-voltage, HTTP 200, 2026-10-03T00:30:20Z)

found_values.value: Found for the design the owner sets: LTC4352CMS#TRPBF with CSD17573Q5B between each TPS55285 output and its rail; OPA376AIDBVR from the 5 V rail compares the rail (332 kOhm / 100 kOhm) with the converter's output (an equal divider returned to 30.4 mV from REF3112AIDBZR), offset 0.1008 V; CSD17578Q3A switches the load resistor. MOSFET drop and loss: the LTC4352 regulates the drop to 25 mV typ, 10 to 40 mV, while I x RDS(on) is lower (9.2 mV at 6.35 A, 1.45 mOhm max at VGS 4.5 V): 0.16 W typ, 0.25 W max at 6.35 A, 0.09 W typ at 3.72 A. Feedback: internal, at the TPS55285's VOUT pin, before the MOSFET; the rail sits 10 to 40 mV below; the cable droop compensation stays off. Turn-off signal and time: the LTC4352 pulls its gate down within 0.5 us max (0.2 us typ, 10 nF, VFWD -0.2 V) once the rail rises above the converter's output; its STATUS open drain, low while the MOSFET is on, releases and lets the op-amp drive the clamp switch. Margin to the ceiling's lowest trip edge: HV -0.128 V with the converter at 8.53 V, +0.032 V at 8.40 V, +0.190 V at 8.27 V (lowest trip 8.534 V); the threshold stays 38 mV under 8.70 V. LV +0.028 to +0.248 V (lowest trip 5.740 V). Energy: not known; peak current threshold / load resistor, 6.37 A at 8.66 V with 1.36 Ohm, 6.36 A at 15.38 V with 2.42 Ohm (stage 2)
found_values.source: Research.md@5f5c0a6 V316; LTC4352 data sheet 4352fa (Rev A 12/10), www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/4352fa.pdf, read 2026-10-03T00:17:03Z; OPA376 SBOS406G (revised December 2015), ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa376.pdf, read 2026-10-03T00:24:22Z; CSD17573Q5B SLPS492B (revised April 2017), ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/csd17573q5b.pdf, read 2026-10-03T00:23:28Z; CSD17578Q3A SLPS525A (revised January 2016), ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/csd17578q3a.pdf, read 2026-10-03T00:23:28Z; SLVSI72A, ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf, read 2026-10-03T00:23:26Z 6.3.11, 6.3.13; model/clamp.py (run 2026-10-03T00:31Z)

Doing so will degrade gain error and increase non-linearity'; the owner's leads are 1 kOhm each, 10 times that. functions: I/O expander
exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: Lines: 16 lines a part at 2 addresses give 32, under 33 (round 1 readings)
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: The 33 comes from Pins.md I/O expanders, which counts two expander inputs for the DC input's source status and brownout 'until a decision lets one signal serve both'. V271 and V276 (owner, 2026-10-01) make that decision: one signal, the DC input voltage through a divider into one ADC input of the measurement coprocessor (GPIO 40 to 47), serving both. The expander then carries 31 lines: 20 port enables, 5 bias selectors (R4's SN74LVC1G126DBVR is driven by a line), 5 converter enables, 1 hardware latch read-back; V316 removed the clamp threshold-select lines. 32 lines are at least 31. The page does not pin the four rail latches' read-back for V283's firmware report; if they took expander lines the count would be 35, so the finding assumes they do not. The datasheets pass the other values. TCA6416A (SCPS205, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tca6416a.pdf, read 2026-10-03T01:00:26Z): active-low RESET returns the registers to default, all 16 P-ports are inputs at power-on and after reset, no internal P-port pull-up, 400 kHz, address 0x20 or 0x21 by ADDR (clear of 0x31, 0x40 to 0x4F, 0x18 to 0x1F and 74h/75h), push-pull outputs that source 10 mA. PCAL6416A (https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/data-sheet/PCAL6416A.pdf, read 2026-10-03T01:13:58Z): 'All I/Os are set to inputs at reset', registers return to default on power-up or reset, same 0x20 or 0x21. JLCPCB need is 2 parts x 5 boards = 10, gate 50: TCA6416APWR C130203 2526/2361, TCA6416ARTWR C182336 12685/12614 (2026-10-03T01:00:35Z and :37Z), PCAL6416AHF,128 C2652287 20572/20503 (2026-10-03T01:00:37Z), all expand. Digi-Key (2026-10-03): TCA6416APWR Active, stock 11812, 20 weeks (01:10:09Z); TCA6416ARTWR Active, stock 0, 20 weeks (01:10:11Z); PCAL6416AHF,128 Active, stock 111866, 30 weeks (01:10:13Z). TCAL6416PWR (JLCPCB C20345827 106/106) is left out of this finding: its feature text says RESET re-initialises the bus 'without resetting the sticky registers' while section 7.3.5 says the registers return to default, a conflict not resolved here.

functions: Servo rail clamp
exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: response: slew 0.16 V/us takes about 16 us to a 2.5 V gate threshold (OPA333 SBOS351E); FU-2H drop, the same reason under V316
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: The Servo rail clamp function states no response-time value: V316 asks for the margin to the ceiling, the turn-off signal and its time, and the clamp switch's response is 'reported' (Servo rail clamp switch). A speed that is stated nowhere is not a requirement value, and OPA376's 2 V/us (about 6 us to the same threshold) is equally unstated. Against the stated values both parts pass with less offset error than OPA376AIDBVR, so P2's 'smallest offset error' for rank 1 is not right. OPA333 (SBOS351, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa333.pdf, read 2026-10-03T01:02:25Z): VOS 10 uV max at 5 V, drift 0.05 uV/degC max, CMRR 106 dB min, input range (V-) - 0.1 to (V+) + 0.1 V (the 3.56 V divided input is inside), 1.8 to 5.5 V supply, -40 to 125 degC. Through P2's own error model (scratch/FU-2I/P2-R6/model/clamp.py with only the op-amp row changed: VOS plus 25 K of drift, CMRR at VCM 3.56 V) the highest thresholds are 8.659 V at the 8.53 V set point (41 mV under 8.70 V, against 38 mV for OPA376) and 5.710 V at 5.59 V (30 mV under the LV ceiling's lowest trip edge 5.740 V, against 28 mV), and the lowest threshold stays above the converter's output at both settings and at 0.8 V. data.ruling:
The refutation stands: both verifiers' refutations hold on re-reading.

1) Stock, sourcing rule 4. JLCPCB's exact LCSC match C2887910 is INA228AIDGSR, Texas Instruments, VSSOP-10. It reads stockCount 0 and canPresaleNumber -254. Rule 4 fails any negative presale count, whatever the stock. The gate is 50 under S4 (5 x need, never under 50) and S7 (5 boards). That holds at this function's 1 placement (need 5) and at the part's 2 a board (need 10, IOBoard.md:465). Stock 0 is under 50. The part is not held: the Held parts table and inventory-2026-09-25.csv have no INA2 row, so rule 6 does not apply. The rule 5 second-vendor route fails too. Digi-Key reads 0 in Tape & Reel, Cut Tape and Digi-Reel, with a 20-week lead time.

2) Datasheet, series resistance. IOBoard.md:464 (decided, owner 2026-09-30, kept by V306) puts 1 kOhm in series with IN+ and with IN-. SLYS021A 8.1.4 says to filter with "the lowest possible series resistance (typically 100 Ω or less)". Below Figure 8-1 it says: "Do not use values greater than 100 ohms for RFILTER. Doing so will degrade gain error and increase non-linearity." The only protection value the sheet gives is 10 Ohm in series with each input. 1 kOhm is 10 times the limit. This alone makes the check fail against the function's decided circuit.

The accuracy check also holds as arithmetic. RDIFF is 92 kOhm typical, with no minimum, maximum or drift (6.5). So 2 x 1 kOhm reads 2/94 = 2.13 % low, typical, and the drift of that error is not bounded. The +/-1 % target is a value found for V166, which is still "for research", not an owner answer. The 2.13 % error and its unbounded drift therefore stand as datasheet facts. The verdict against a requirement rests on point 2's maker limit.

The other checks pass and are not disputed: TI ACTIVE, Digi-Key Active, end_of_life false, Texas Instruments on S1, LCSC identity correct, and the first datasheet revision January 2021. No part-level cause fails. The stock gate is a quantity gate, and the 1 kOhm conflict belongs to this function's own sense circuit, so the scope is function. This matches FU-2G/011 on the same function and FU-2H/013 on stock scope. FU-2B2/015 and FU-2G/010 ruled part on stock, so earlier rulings split.

The INA228 is the owner's fixed input (Scope, Fixed inputs; V304). A fixed input that fails a check is reported to the owner, not re-selected. V304 makes the stock failure a current limitation and a T6 stock exception. It does not make rule 4 pass. The owner has to resolve the clash between the datasheet's 100 Ohm limit and the decided 1 kOhm.

No replacement goes to new verifiers. The relayed question on V318, an 18 V input with a TVS under 27 V, is R5's and is recorded as V319. This R8 ruling does not answer it.

data.ruling:
The datasheet verifier's refutation stands, on the critical pin hold check. The stock verifier confirmed every figure and refuted nothing.

The function's decided behaviour is in IOBoard.md, Current aborts, and in the Servo current ceiling row (owner, 2026-09-30):
- Each INA3221's Critical output carries the 3.0 A abort.
- The main coprocessor aborts only when the line stays low longer than a blanking time.
- A shorter trip is logged, not an abort.

V287 (for research, owner 2026-10-01) asks for that blanking time against the INA3221's conversion time. Setting it needs one fact: how long the transparent Critical pin stays low under a sustained over-limit current on one channel while three channels convert in turn. SBOS576C does not state this. I re-read the datasheet at its source:
- 7.3.2.1 says only when the pin pulls low.
- Table 8-34 defines CEN = 0 only as "Transparent (default)".
- The only release wording, 7.5.3, applies to Latch mode.
- The application example, 9.2.1 Table 9-1, enables CH1 alone, so Figures 9-2 and 9-3 cannot show how three channels share the pin.

The datasheet does not rule out one reading: the pin follows each conversion of any channel. Under that reading, a sustained fault on one of three shunt-only channels holds the line low for 1.1 ms typical and 1.21 ms maximum in every 3.3 to 3.63 ms. The cases then fail as follows:
- A blanking time above 1.21 ms never fires, so the 3.0 A abort never happens.
- A blanking time below one conversion blanks nothing, which defeats the owner's logged-not-aborted rule for a servo charging its capacitors.

So the maker's documents cannot show that the part meets the function's abort requirement. A part qualified on that behaviour would rest on an assumption. Two TI E2E threads (TI's support forum), which are secondary sources and not maker figures, leave the point open:
- 807608: a TI engineer says the pin restores "after one conversion", without naming whose. A customer saw Ch.1 low for "6 channels sampled x 8.24ms", with the alert mode not stated.
- 1625525: a TI engineer says the alert clears "as soon as the shunt voltage drops back down", with no multi-channel case.

The FU-2H adjudicator rulings 016 and 017 held the same release point as not read. No owner answer under Raised by P1 has settled it since, and V287 is the last INA3221 entry. Either of two things closes it: a bench measurement of the Critical pin with 3 channels enabled and one over the limit, or TI's statement of the release point. An owner decision that changes the abort scheme would also close it, for example latch mode cleared by the measurement coprocessor, or counting lows in a window. That decision is the owner's, not this ruling's.

The scope is the function. Lifecycle (ACTIVE at TI, Active at Digi-Key), end-of-life notices (none), LCSC identity (C181255) and the S1 (sourcing rule 1) allowlist (Texas Instruments) all pass. The fault is the fit of this function's alert timing.

The relayed V318/V319 question, 18 V in place of 20 V against 27 V, concerns R5's bus. It does not touch this ruling. The port monitors sit on servo rails of 8.4 V at most, and their 26 V input rating passes either way.
data.evidence: SBOS576C (MAY 2012, revised SEPTEMBER 2026). 7.3.2.1: "The Critical alert pin pulls low if any channel measurement exceeds the limit present in the corresponding-channel critical-alert limit register." No sentence states when the pin releases. Table 8-34, bit 10 CEN: "Critical alert latch enable ... 0 = Transparent (default), 1 = Latch enabled". CF1-3 "are cleared when the Mask/Enable register is read back", which says nothing about the pin. 7.5.3: "continues to hold the alert line low until the interrupt is cleared. Alerts must be in Latch mode to function." 9.2.1 Table 9-1: "Enabled channel CH1", operating mode "Shunt voltage, continuous". 9.2.2: "the Critical alert pin pulls low after the conversion cycle completes", for 1.1 ms and 588 us. 6.5: tCONVERT at CT=100 is 1.1 ms typical and 1.21 ms maximum, with no minimum. 7.4.2.1: shunt-only mode on 3 channels puts two other conversions between repeats of one channel. A text search of the datasheet for latch, release, clears and deassert finds no release condition for the transparent Critical pin. TI E2E 807608, TI engineer: "If the Critical pin is set to transparent mode, after the over limit condition is removed, the Critical pin should restore automatically after one conversion." Customer, same thread: "The Critical flag (Ch.1) remains active for 50ms (6 channels sampled x 8.24ms)", with the mode not stated. TI E2E 1625525, TI engineer: "As soon as the shunt voltage drops back down below the programmed level, the alert clears." Neither thread covers three enabled channels. Requirement: IOBoard.md, Current aborts (row at :113) and Servo current ceiling (:389); Research.md V287 (:1000) and the Follow-ups row (:594). Earlier rulings: round2/FU-2H/016-adjudicator-R8-3.json and 017-adjudicator-R8-4.json, both stands true, scope function.

data.ruling: The refutation stands, scope function. The figure says "No R8 requirement value changes", and that is false. V171 is a value found for research. Its owner answer is "for research (owner, 2026-09-28)". The last P2 to find it, FU-2H, set the Port current monitor's input withstand to 20 V, "the top of the DC input". FU-2H's datasheet verifier confirmed it against "Scope: 12 to 20 V DC input". V319 replaces 12 to 20 V with 12 to 18 V. That moves the Port current monitor's input withstand requirement from 20 V to 18 V. The figure states that 18 V withstand itself, so it contradicts its own opening sentence. The rest of the figure holds. INA3221 SBOS576C 6.1 rates the IN+ and IN- common mode at -0.3 to 26 V, 8 V above 18 V. The 27 V bus hold of V318 is 1 V above 26 V. The INA228s sit on the ESC pack side. The conclusion therefore stands: lowering the DC input to 18 V keeps every R8 part inside its rating under a single fault. Only the "no requirement value changes" statement is refuted. The change relaxes the requirement, from 20 V to 18 V, and no R8 part fails because of it.

data.function: re-rank report: WSBS8518L1000JK35 status at Digi-Key
data.ruling: The refutation stands. The reading is right, but the conclusion drawn from it is not. Digi-Key lists WSBS8518L1000JK35 (Vishay Dale) with ProductStatus 'Discontinued at DigiKey', stock 50 and a lead time of 48 weeks. Vishay's product page for the WSBS8518 carries no status for each part number in its body. So the Lifecycle check (owner, 2026-10-02) reads Digi-Key's ProductStatus in its place. Under that rule, Active passes. Not For New Designs, Last Time Buy and Obsolete fail, and Preliminary fails under S5. 'Any other value is recorded and reported to the owner.' 'Discontinued at DigiKey' is a value outside that list. It describes Digi-Key's own stocking, and the same API record has discontinued=false and end_of_life=false. So JK35 neither passes nor fails the lifecycle gate: its status is recorded and reported to the owner. The claim 'fails the lifecycle gate, so WSBS8518L1000JT35 has no rule 5 alternate' does not follow. Its stock of 50 is at the rule 4 gate of 50.
data.evidence: Digi-Key keyword search 'WSBS8518L1000' (--limit 50, cached, 20 products). WSBS8518L1000JK35, Vishay Dale: status 'Discontinued at DigiKey', stock_available 50, lead_weeks 48, discontinued false, end_of_life false, https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/vishay-dale/WSBS8518L1000JK35/6709546. The other 19 WSBS8518L1000 variants are Active, among them JT35 (stock 79) and JK34 (stock 97). Vishay's product page https://www.vishay.com/en/product/30134/ (HTTP 200, 765413 bytes, read 2026-10-03T01:36:18Z) does not name WSBS8518L1000 or JK35 anywhere in its body (0 matches) and carries no lifecycle status. The Vishay search URL for WSBS8518L1000JK35 returned HTTP 500 at 2026-10-03T01:36:12Z. Research.md, Lifecycle check, Manufacturer status row: where a product page carries no status in its body, Digi-Key's ProductStatus is read in its place. Its gate lists the failing ProductStatus values as Not For New Designs, Last Time Buy and Obsolete, plus Preliminary under S5. 'Any other value is recorded and reported to the owner.'

data.ruling: The refutation stands on point (2). Point (1) holds in part. The claim quotes 'auch nicht kurzzeitig' (not even briefly) from SLS_Sicherheitshinweise_DE_A4.pdf section 4. That section does not contain the words. Section 4 says only 'nie unter 3,3 V pro Zelle'. The words appear in the same shop's LiPoFAQV15c.pdf, in the paragraph 'Zusammenfassend'. The upper bound on the filter rests on this quote, so as written the figure cites a source that does not carry it. The substance can be restated with LiPoFAQV15c as its source. Point (1): SLUUBT5C, note after 3.1, says a 1 s granularity delay 'can have an average trigger delay equal to the delay setting plus 1.5 s'. At CUV:Delay 0 s that is an average of 1.5 s. The Technical Reference Manual (TRM) states no maximum. 'Triggers on average within up to 1.5 s' is acceptable as a statement about the average. It is not a bound on any single trip, and the figure must not use it as one. CUV:Delay is confirmed as U1, 0 to 255 s, default 2 s (TRM 19.10.1.2). The ruling concerns how this figure is sourced and worded. It does not concern any part, so scope is function.
data.evidence: SLS_Sicherheitshinweise_DE_A4.pdf, section '4. Betrieb und Entladung', text extracted with pdftotext: 'Entladeschluss: Entladen Sie den Akku unter Last nie unter 3,3 V pro Zelle. Im Ruhezustand sollte die Spannung pro Zelle nicht unter 3,75 V fallen'. In the whole document 'kurzzeitig' appears once, at the 60C discharge rating in section 3. LiPoFAQV15c.pdf, 'Zusammenfassend:': 'Entladen Sie den Akku unter Last nie tiefer als 3,3V pro Zelle, auch nicht kurzzeitig.' TRM SLUUBT5C (Nov 2018, rev. June 2021), Note after 3.1: 'A delay setting with 1-s granularity can have an average trigger delay equal to the delay setting plus 1.5 s.' No maximum delay is stated. 3.2 Trip: 'Min cell voltage1..7 <= CUV:Threshold for CUV:Delay duration'. 19.10.1.2 Protections/CUV/Delay: Type U1, Min 0, Max 255, Default 2, Unit s.

data.ruling: The refutation stands. The figure is incomplete. The kept part for R5's encoder 12 V supply is TPS55288RPMR (selection.json, run FU-2H, rank 1; the FU-2I re-rank keeps it at rank 1). That part integrates only the two boost-leg MOSFETs. Its buck leg is two external N-channel MOSFETs, driven from DR1H (pin 2) and DR1L (pin 1). Round 2's stage 1 rules leave "the MOSFETs that R5's and R7's controllers drive" to stage 2, and they require P2 to state those MOSFETs' requirements: drain-source voltage, share of the drop allowance, safe operating area and body-diode current. The TPS55288 is an R5 controller that drives MOSFETs. The figure names only the LM74800 DC path, the pack path and the BQ40Z80 CHG/DSG sets, so stage 2 gets no requirement for the two buck-leg MOSFETs, and no stage 1 function selects them. The parenthetical in the rule (the LM74800's, the pack protector's and the charger's) gives examples. It does not narrow the rule's set: the rule is stated as the MOSFETs R5's and R7's controllers drive. The P2 encoder entry is wrong at the root of the omission: it calls the TPS55288 a "buck-boost with integrated switches". The verifier's remark about the ISP-ISN sense resistor concerns a resistor, which goes to stage 2 by type. It does not bear on this figure, and the ruling does not rest on it. The verifier found the LM74800 and BQ40Z80 values consistent with their datasheets, and this ruling does not dispute them. Scope is function: what fails is the completeness of R5's stage 2 MOSFET requirement list, not any part's identity, lifecycle or maker. The ruling leaves V319's 18 V cut-off and the bus-clamp figure untouched. The missing entry is for the buck-leg pair on the TPS55288's VIN. Its VDS must cover the bus that VIN sits on, the same bus the TPS55285 sees (V318, V319).
data.evidence: The TPS55288 datasheet SLVSF01B (Nov 2018, revised Dec 2020) states three things. Section 3 Description: "The TPS55288 integrates two 16-A MOSFETs of the boost leg to balance the solution size and efficiency." Section 5 pin table: pin 1 DR1L is the "Gate driver output for low-side MOSFET in buck side", and pin 2 DR1H is the "Gate driver output for high-side MOSFET in buck side". Section 7.3.13 Integrated Gate Drivers: "In buck operation, the DR1H pin and the DR1L pin are switched by the PWM controller." Section 6.5 lists DR1H and DR1L gate-driver drops of 0.1 V sinking and 0.2 V sourcing at 100 mA. selection.json gives the encoder 12 V supply as TPS55288RPMR, rank 1, run FU-2H. The FU-2I P2-R5 return figure "MOSFETs for stage 2" lists only the LM74800 DC path, the LM74800 pack path, and the BQ40Z80 CHG and DSG. Its encoder entry reads "buck-boost with integrated switches". The FU-2I re-rank's rank 2, TPS552882RPMR, is credited with "two external buck-leg MOSFETs" while rank 1 is still called integrated. data.function: re-rank report: LM74910 / LM74900 overvoltage band
data.ruling: The refutation stands, but only on the figure's last sentence. The LM74910 / LM74900 band itself reproduces. With 59.7 kOhm over 2.00 kOhm, 0.1 % resistors, I(OV) 200 nA and R(SW) 10 to 46 Ohm, the trip is 18.0034 to 19.4996 V and the release is 16.402 to 17.736 V. That leaves 3.4 mV over the 18.0 V floor and 0.39 mV under the 19.5 V ceiling. The comparison sentence is wrong. It says "The LM74800 has 0.45 V and 0.23 V of margin at the same two ends." FU-2I's own LM74800 design (P2 ratio 15.159, 0.1 % resistors, 2 mV leakage term) trips at 18.051 / 18.661 / 19.273 V. Its margin over the 18.0 V floor (V319) is therefore 0.051 V, not 0.45 V. The 0.23 V margin under the TVS1800's 19.5 V minimum breakdown is correct. No LM74800 margin of 0.45 V appears at these two ends in any FU-2H or FU-2I record. The figure as reported misstates how much wider the LM74800's low-end margin is than the LM74910's, and the reports use that margin to compare the two candidates. The scope is the function, because the error lies in this report's arithmetic against this function's floor and ceiling and not in either part.
data.evidence: LM7480-Q1 SNOSD95C section 7.5: V(OVR) 1.195 / 1.231 / 1.267 V, V(OVF) 1.091 / 1.13 / 1.159 V, I(OV) 53 nA typical and 200 nA maximum, R(SW) 10 / 19.5 / 46 Ohm. LM74910-Q1 SNOSDE6C section 6.5: V(OVR) 0.585 / 0.6 / 0.63 V, V(OVF) 0.533 / 0.55 / 0.573 V, I(OV) 50 nA typical and 200 nA maximum, R(SW) 10 / 22.5 / 46 Ohm. All of these match the claim and the verifier. The FU-2I P2 calculation (scratch/FU-2I/P2-R5/calc.py), re-run, gives an LM74800 ratio of 15.159 with a band of 15.1307 to 15.1873. That puts the trip at 18.051 / 18.661 / 19.273 V and the release at 16.477 / 17.13 / 17.633 V. The margins are 18.051 - 18.0 = 0.051 V and 19.5 - 19.273 = 0.227 V. The FU-2I re-rank's own final.json gives the same LM74800 trip in its rank-1 reasons ("trip 18.05 / 18.66 / 19.27 V, 0.23 V under the TVS1800's 19.5 V minimum breakdown"). The LM74910 calculation (scratch/FU-2I/P4-datasheet-R5/calc2.py), re-run, gives (18.00335, 19.49961, 16.40199, 17.73645) V, with margins of 0.00335 V and 0.00039 V. In FU-2H, the LM74800 band was 20.35 to 21.66 V against a 20.0 to 22.0 V window, which gives margins of 0.35 V and 0.34 V. So 0.45 V is not an LM74800 margin at either the current ends or the earlier ones. The requirement is Research.md V319 (owner, 2026-10-03): the cut-off trips above 18 V. The 19.5 V ceiling is the TVS1800's minimum breakdown.

data.function: re-rank report: TPS552882 against the TPS55288
data.ruling: The refutation stands. The claim says the TPS552882 adds two buck-leg MOSFETs and a sense resistor, "against none for the TPS55288". That is false. The TPS55288 integrates only the boost-leg MOSFETs. Its buck leg is two external MOSFETs driven from DR1H and DR1L, and its ISP/ISN output-current sense resistor is external too. The TPS552882 has the same external buck leg and the same optional ISP/ISN sense resistor. Both parts need the same external power parts. They differ in the I2C interface (SCL and SDA on pins 5 and 6 of the TPS55288; none on the TPS552882) and in how the TPS552882 is set without registers. The rest of the claim was not refuted and matches SLVSFC5: VIN 2.7 to 36 V, VIN and SW1 40 V absolute maximum, no I2C. The scope is function. The error is in this re-rank's comparison of external part count for the encoder 12 V supply, not in either part's lifecycle or identity.
data.evidence: TPS55288 SLVSF01B (Rev. B, December 2020), section 3: "The TPS55288 integrates two 16-A MOSFETs of the boost leg." Section 7.1: "a 16-A buck-boost DC-to-DC converter with the two boost MOSFETs integrated." Table 5-1: pin 1 DR1L "Gate driver output for low-side MOSFET in buck side", pin 2 DR1H "Gate driver output for high-side MOSFET in buck side". The BOOT1 description refers to "the source of external high-side power MOSFET". The ISP and ISN pins take "an optional current sense resistor" to limit the output current. Pins 5 and 6 are SCL and SDA. TPS552882 SLVSFC5 (November 2020), section 3: "integrates two 16-A MOSFETs of the boost leg". Table 5-1: pins 1 and 2 are DR1L and DR1H, the buck-side gate drivers. The block diagram shows DR1H, DR1L, BOOT1 and SW1. ISP and ISN take the same optional sense resistor. Section 6.1: VIN and SW1 are rated -0.3 to 40 V. The two parts need the same external MOSFET and sense-resistor count, so the claim's "against none for the TPS55288" is wrong.

data.function: P2 report: Servo rail clamp response and overshoot
data.ruling: The refutation stands. The claim says its response times start at the threshold and include the op-amp's 0.33 us overload recovery and its 2 V/us slew. They do not. CSD17578Q3A: 3.1 us to conduction and 15.6 us to 4.5 V. NTTFS4C10NTAG: 1.9 us and 9.8 us. Each of these is the 3.92 kOhm gate RC driven by an instant 4.9 V step, with no recovery and no slew (clamp.py, response block). With both included, the CSD17578Q3A gate reaches VGS(th) max 1.9 V at 4.65 us and 4.5 V at 17.21 us after the threshold. The NTTFS4C10NTAG gate gets there at 3.53 us and 11.37 us, using its 993 pF typical Ciss, as the datasheet gives no maximum. So the response times are understated by 1.6 us to conduction on both parts and by 1.6 to 1.6 us to full enhancement. The overshoot figures were computed over 17 us, not over the stated 15.6 us, so the claim contradicts itself. They match the corrected time to within rounding: 0.108 V into 1000 uF, 0.230 V into 470 uF and 1.08 V into 100 uF at 17 us, against 0.109 V, 0.233 V and 1.09 V at 17.2 us. The overshoot values hold. The response-time values in the figure do not. This concerns the figure in this function, not any part's lifecycle or identity, so the scope is function.
data.evidence:
Datasheet values re-read. OPA376 (SBOS406G), Electrical Characteristics: slew rate 2 V/us typical at G=1, overload recovery time 0.33 us typical. CSD17578Q3A (SLPS525A, revised January 2016), section 5.1: VGS(th) 1.1 / 1.5 / 1.9 V min/typ/max at VDS = VGS and ID = 250 uA; Ciss 1150 pF typical, 1590 pF maximum. NTTFS4C10N/D: Ciss 993 pF typical, no maximum; VGS(TH) 1.3 to 2.2 V.

Model re-run at 2026-10-03T02:18:36Z. P2's clamp.py is identical to the verifier's copy, which `diff` confirms. It computes tau x ln(4.9/(4.9 - Vg)) with tau = 3.92 kOhm x 1.59 nF = 6.23 us. That gives 3.06 us at 1.9 V and 15.62 us at 4.5 V, and 1.91 us and 9.75 us for the NTTFS4C10NTAG. These are the claimed values, and the formula has no delay term and no ramp term.

The verifier's resp.py, a 1 ns Euler step with a 0.33 us delay and a 2 V/us ramp to 4.9 V, gives 1.9 V at 4.7 us and 4.5 V at 17.2 us. My own closed-form first-order solution (ramp, then hold, into the RC) gives the same: 4.65 us and 17.21 us for the CSD17578Q3A, and 3.53 us and 11.37 us for the NTTFS4C10NTAG.

Overshoot, I x t / C at 6.35 A:
- over 17 us: 0.108 V into 1000 uF, 0.230 V into 470 uF, 1.079 V into 100 uF
- over 17.2 us: 0.109 V, 0.233 V and 1.09 V

The owner has made that decision. It adds no expander line. The scope is function: the count is about this function's requirement, not about the MCP23017 itself.

data.function: re-rank report: Servo rail clamp op-amps: response and error budget
data.ruling: The refutation stands. The figure gives TLV9001 gate times of 4.3 us to 1.9 V and 16.9 us to 4.5 V. These omit TLV9001's stated overload recovery, while OPA376 gets its 0.33 us in the same model. Section 7.10 of the TLV9001 data sheet (SBOS833R, revised November 2021) lists tOR, the overload recovery time, as 0.85 us typical at VS 5 V with VIN x gain > VS. Section 8.4 says the delay after overload is the recovery time plus the slew time, about 850 ns. The figure's label "recovery not stated" is therefore wrong. Re-running P3's own resp.py with a 0.85 us delay for TLV9001 gives 5.2 us to 1.9 V and 17.7 us to 4.5 V. Rail rise at 6.35 A is then 0.113 V into 1000 uF and 1.13 V into 100 uF. On those times TLV9001 is slower than OPA376 (4.7 and 17.2 us), not faster. The figure states that the ranking rests on the response, so the error changes the ranking basis. The scope is function: the defect is in this function's response budget, not in the part's lifecycle or identity. The other values reproduce. OPA376 gives 4.7 and 17.2 us, rising 0.109 V into 1000 uF and 1.09 V into 100 uF. OPA333 and TLV333 give 17.7 and 36.3 us, rising 0.230 V into 1000 uF and 2.30 V into 100 uF. Their data sheets show overvoltage recovery only as plots (OPA333 Figures 12 and 13, TLV333 Figures 11 and 12), with no tabulated time. Their 0 us delay is therefore unchanged, and how much recovery would add for them is not read.
data.evidence: TLV9001 data sheet SBOS833R, 7.10 Electrical Characteristics: "SR Slew rate VS = 5 V 2 V/us" and "tOR Overload recovery time VS = 5 V, VIN x gain > VS 0.85 us". Section 8.4: "the propagation delay (in case of an overload condition) is the sum of the overload recovery time and the slew time. The overload recovery time for the TLV900x family is approximately 850 ns." OPA376 data sheet: "Overload recovery time VIN x gain > VS 0.33 us". scratch/FU-2I/rerank-R6/resp.py runs TLV9001 with delay 0.0, labelled "recovery not stated". The re-run copy, scratch/FU-2I/adjudicator-R6/resp_adj.py, gave these times to 1.1, 1.9 and 4.5 V. TLV9001 with 0.85 us: 3.7, 5.2 and 17.7 us, rising 0.113 V into 1000 uF and 1.13 V into 100 uF. TLV9001 with no recovery: 2.9, 4.3 and 16.9 us, as the figure states. OPA376 with 0.33 us: 3.2, 4.7 and 17.2 us. OPA333 and TLV333: 12.2, 17.7 and 36.3 us.
